records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit. When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Section 3 describe these exact interactions across decode, execution completion, decode decay ticks, and SC LSUM integration.

records.claim: Total storage for sR is 53,863 bits (43,008 bits WT + 9,360 bits UT + 1,495 bits status table).
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Matches the exact component bit counts and sum of 53,863 bits given in Table 3 for sR.

records.claim: INT register digest generation XOR-folds trailing count [5:0], leading count [8:3], and value LSBs [11:6], mapping 0x8 to digest 0x3E3.
records.quote: For integer registers, the digest encodes the count of leading zeros (or ones), the count of trailing zeros (or ones), and the six least significant bits, effectively capturing characteristics of addresses and round numbers.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(a) establish that the three 6-bit fields are XOR-folded into a 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Condition flag digest generation replicates 4 flag bits three times to form a 12-bit digest, mapping 0x9 to 0x999.
records.quote: For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(c) define replicating Value[3:0] three times across the 12-bit digest.

records.claim: FP32 digest generation extracts bits [31:26] and places them at digest bits [8:3], mapping 0x2B to 0x158.
records.quote: For floating-point registers, we inspect the most significant bits to classify the format and then extract the sign bit along with the most significant bits of the exponent.
records.why: Section 4.2 and Figure 6(b) define extracting Value[31:26] into digest bits [8:3].

records.claim: stale_digest_invalidation_after_256_instructions specifies decay_ctr initialized to 256.
records.quote: { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65
records.why: Table 3 declares decay_ctr as an 8-bit counter, which cannot store 256; tracking 256 elapsed instructions requires initializing the 8-bit counter to 255.

value.name: stale_digest_invalidation_after_256_instructions
value.given: Register R4 is written and marked valid with 8-bit decay_ctr initialized to 255. 256 subsequent instructions are decoded without further writes to R4.
value.expect: On the 256th decode step, R4 decay_ctr expires and valid bit is cleared to 0.

records.claim: Bank output is suppressed to 0 if bank usefulness is non-positive, and scaled by 2.5 if positive.
records.quote: Figure 5 shows the structure of the SC in RUNLTS.
records.why: Figure 5(c) illustrates per-bank usefulness gating with the multiplier stage labeled 'x0 or x2.5'.

records.claim: Values produced by instructions completing during wrong-path execution remain valid after branch recovery to assist subsequent predictions.
records.quote: By leveraging these extra values after the flush, our scheme can correct subsequent mispredictions starting with the second one.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes how instructions completing ahead in the pipeline preserve valid digests after a flush.
